passages.original: Dominus dicit in Evangelio : Omnem decimationem vestram distribuite. Ipse per prophetam loquitur : Inferte omnem decimam in horreum meum, ut sit ci- bus in domo mia, et probate me in his, dicit Dominus. Paulus apostolus dixit de filiis Levi : Sacerdotium accipientes, mandatum habent decimas sumere a populo secundum legem, id est a fratribus suis; hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus. Salomon dixit : Alii dividunt propria et diriores fiunt : alii. rapiunt non sua, et semper in egestate sunt (Prov. XI). Jesus lilius Sira< h dixit : In omni dato, hilarem fac tultum mum, et in ersultatione sanctifica decimas tuas. Da Altissimo secundum datum, et in bono oculo ad nventionem facito manuum tuarum, quoniam D ininus retribuens est, ei septies tantum reddet tibi. Augustinus dixit ; Decimæ etenim tributa sunt egentium animarum b Quod si decimam dederis, non solum abundantiam frugum recipies, scJ etiam sanitatem corporum consequeris. Non eget Dominus Deus, non præmium postulat, sed honorme ;
passages.english: The Lord says in the Gospel: "Distribute all your tithing." He himself speaks through the prophet: "Bring every tithe into my storehouse, so that there may be food in my house, and test me in these things, says the Lord." Paul the apostle said of the sons of Levi: "Those who receive the priesthood have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, from their brothers"; for "God loves a cheerful giver." Solomon said: "Some divide what is their own and become richer; others seize what is not theirs and are always in want" (Prov. 11). Jesus son of Sirach said: "In every gift make your face cheerful, and in rejoicing sanctify your tithes. Give to the Most High according to what has been given, and with a good eye make [your offering] according to the finding of your hands, for the Lord is one who repays, and he will give back to you seven times as much." Augustine said: "For tithes are the tributes of needy souls. And if you give the tithe, you will not only receive an abundance of crops, but you will also obtain health of bodies. The Lord God is not in need, he does not demand a reward, but honour."
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected silently: 'mia' for 'mea', 'diriores' for 'ditiores', 'lilius Sira< h' for 'filius Sirach', 'tultum mum' for 'vultum tuum', 'ersultatione' for 'exsultatione', 'nventionem' for 'adinventionem', 'D ininus' for 'Dominus', 'ei' for 'et', 'scJ' for 'sed', 'honorme' for 'honorem'. A stray footnote mark 'b' omitted. 'ad adinventionem manuum tuarum' (Sirach) is obscure; rendered literally as 'according to the finding of your hands', i.e. according to what your hands have gained. The passage ends mid-thought; the sentence continues in the following text.

passages.original: Nemo se circumveniat, fratres : omnis homo qui post baptismum mortalia crimina commiserit, hoc est homicidium, adulterium, furtum, falsum testimonium, vel reliqua crimina perpetraverit, unde per legem mundanam mori poterat, si pœnitentiam non egerit, eleemosynam justam non fecerit, nunquam habebit vitam æternam, sed cum diabolo descendet in tormenta. Proinde beatus Isidorus dicit : Nunquam Deus delinquentibus parcet, quoniam peccatores ideo flagelio temporali non castigat, ut in judicium aeternum punicndos relinquat; ac proinde est quod Dominus delinquentibus non parcet. Et beatus Augustinus dicit : Nulla peccata dimittit Deus inulta : hoc est, invindicata. Aut certe nos ,indi amus per pœnitentiam, aut certe vindicab t illa Deus per severitatem judicii, qua dicturus erit: Discedite a me, maledicti, in ignem æternum (Matth. XXV). Et illa, certissime cresite, fratres, quod omnis homo quamvis peccator, quamvis criminosus sit, quantalibet mala perpetraverit, si poenitentiam egerit et eleemosynam justam fecerit, nunquam descendet in infernum, sed ah angelis elevabitur in cœlum. Unde Dominus dicit : Non judicatur homo bis in idipsum a. Apostolus dicit: Quod si nos judicamus, a Domino non judicamur; hoc est : ille qi in præsenti vita semetipsum per pœnitentiam judicat, ad judicium iterum non rejudicalur, quia hic in præsenti vita terminatur.
passages.english: Let no one deceive himself, brothers: every person who after baptism has committed mortal crimes, that is, murder, adultery, theft, false witness, or has perpetrated the other crimes for which he could be put to death under worldly law, if he has not done penance and has not given just alms, will never have eternal life, but will go down with the devil into torments. Accordingly the blessed Isidore says: "God will never spare those who do wrong, since the reason he does not chastise sinners with temporal punishment is that he may leave them to be punished in the eternal judgement; and so it is that the Lord will not spare those who do wrong." And the blessed Augustine says: "God forgives no sins unpunished", that is, unavenged. Either we ourselves avenge them through penance, or God will certainly avenge them through the severity of the judgement, in which he will say: "Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire" (Matt. 25). And believe this too most certainly, brothers: that every person, however much a sinner, however criminal he may be, whatever evils he has perpetrated, if he has done penance and given just alms, will never go down into hell, but will be raised by the angels into heaven. Hence the Lord says: "A person is not judged twice for the same thing." The Apostle says: "But if we judge ourselves, we are not judged by the Lord"; that is, he who in the present life judges himself through penance is not judged again at the judgement, because here, in the present life, [the matter] is brought to an end.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'flagelio' (flagello), 'punicndos' (puniendos), 'nos ,indi amus' (nos vindicamus), 'vindicab t' (vindicabit), 'cresite' (credite), 'ah' (ab), 'qi' (qui), 'rejudicalur' (rejudicatur); stray footnote mark 'a' omitted. The 'not judged twice' saying is attributed to the Lord but is not a Gospel text (cf. Nahum 1:9 in the Old Latin/Septuagint tradition).
